newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: France says Turkey should be EU member one day.
newsitem.headline: France says Turkey should be EU member one day.

text.p: France said on Sunday that Turkey should one day become a member of the European Union and that a message should be sent to Ankara making this abundantly clear.

Speaking to reporters at an informal EU foreign ministers meeting, France's Herve de Charette distanced his country sharply from a number of its EU partners whose leaders have recently ruled out Turkey joining the European club.
"Turkey has the right to join the EU and that right has to be confirmed forcefully," de Charette said.
In early March, leaders of Europe's Christian Democrat parties stunned many of their partners and the United States by ruling out Turkish EU membership in the short and long term.
The leaders included German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, Spanish Prime Minister Jose-Maria Aznar and Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi.
Sources said the leaders had been furious about Turkish threats to block the enlargement of NATO unless it was made an EU member.
De Charette dismissed suggestions from vaious EU capitals that Turkey's Moslem religion was one of the reasons for keeping it outside the EU.
"We can only judge the membership of a country on objective criteria, and certainly not on religious or ethnic criteria," he said.

Britain was also keen to distance itself from any anti-Turkish stance. "The U.K. believes that Turkey's aspiration for EU membership has to be taken seriously," one senior British official said. "We don't believe in a higher hurdle for Turkey than for others."
Officials said, however, that Turkey was still a long way from becoming a member of the EU because of its economic state and its human-rights record.
De Charette said France would like to include Turkey in a Europe Conference, a forum discussed by EU ministers as a way of keeping countries not yet ready for EU membership close to the bloc.
